newsitem.title: USA: Ex-wife of US Sen. Kerry fights annulment - report.
newsitem.headline: Ex-wife of US Sen. Kerry fights annulment - report.

text.p: The ex-wife of Sen. John Kerry is contesting his request for an annulment of their marriage, the second former spouse of Massachusetts politician to challenge the Catholic Church, the Boston Herald reported Thursday.
Julia Thorne formally stated her opposition to the annulment in a February letter to the church, sources told the newspaper.
Kerry, a Democrat, defeated Republican Gov. William Weld last November in a high-profile Senate battle and has been mentioned by some as a possible presidential candidate in 2000.
The ex-wife of Representative Joseph Kennedy, the son of slain former Attorney General Robert Kennedy, also has expressed her her opposition to their marriage annulment.
Sheila Rauch Kennedy wrote about her opposition in her book "Shattered Faith," to be published in May, and is also fighting their annulment.
The Catholic Church considers marriage a sacramental union that cannot be ended without a grant of annulment, essentially a finding by the church that the marriage never existed.
Kerry's office issued a statement to answer questions about the annulment, the Herald reported.
"Senator Kerry very much understands Julia's feelings and appreciates her support," the statement said. "Senator Kerry believes this is a private family matter."
Kerry and Thorne were married in 1970 and divorced in 1988. He married Teresa Heinz, who inherited part of the ketchup empire when her husband died.
Thorne wrote in her letter to the church that she supports Kerry and his new marriage, but opposes the Catholic view that an annulment would invalidate their 18-year marriage.
